prose_updates.tldr: The constructive side is now an exact finite-horizon radius-aware certificate: optimize the audited Markov truncated Horvitz--Thompson bound over integer windows and cap it by the zero estimator's \(4B^2\) risk.  The certified window is constant when \(C/B\) is below the \(T^{-1/2}\) elbow, has scale \(\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\) in the intermediate regime, and saturates at the horizon when \(C/B\) reaches order \(T^\beta\).  The policy-uniform converse remains open: the common-null calculations do not yet prove even the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) multiscale certificate, so the displayed matched frontier is explicitly conditional.  The \(C=0\) boundary retains the ordinary parametric frontier.

project_justification.gap: Finite-order regular-design optimization, geometric-mixing analyses, and recent sequential rerandomization do not supply a policy-uniform common-null information certificate for fixed-array polynomial memory.  The optimized Markov construction gives a radius-aware all-horizon upper certificate, but no proved deterministic occupancy--information inequality currently rules out a better outcome-adaptive policy, even with the candidate dyadic logarithmic loss.
project_justification.niche: Known beta removes adaptation to the decay index from scope and makes the candidate oracle tradeoff explicit: for the constructive nonadaptive design, exposure variance grows with the homogeneous-history window while deterministic carryover bias decays polynomially; whether outcome-adaptive assignment can beat this tradeoff is exactly the open sequential multiscale-certificate question.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution in the present core is the optimized radius-aware Markov certificate, including the trivial bounded-parameter cap and the low-, intermediate-, and high-memory elbows.  The common-null horizon-eight calculation isolates the prospective converse mechanism, while the general all-policy multiscale certificate and both its logarithmic and no-log forms remain open rather than being promoted as results.

prose_updates.related_work: Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao analyze exact-\(m\), regular switchback designs and optimize Horvitz--Thompson risk; their result informs the constructive architecture here but is not an all-policy or arbitrary-estimator converse.  Hu and Wager study geometrically mixing Markov dynamics, whose stochastic contraction does not imply the fixed-array polynomial-memory certificate sought here.  Jia, Kallus, and Yu provide a truncated-exposure estimation template under rapid mixing and graph clustering, again informing the upper audit rather than the open converse.  Duchi and Ruan's constrained-risk inequality can be used only after close adaptive trajectory laws have been constructed and supplies no switchback occupancy inequality.  Zeng and coauthors study sequential rerandomization under no or first-order carryover.  Xiong, Chin, and Taylor inform the operational window interpretation.  Lin and Ding and Liu and Zhong address separate inference problems.  None of these comparisons is used to claim that the open all-policy multiscale certificate has been proved.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a pre-registered experiment with known \(B\), \(C\), and \(\beta\), the constructive recommendation is to minimize the displayed finite list of \(T\) audited certificates.  In the intermediate regime this means a clock-time window proportional to \(d\{(C/B)^2T\}^{1/(2\beta+1)}\); weak memory calls for a constant window, while sufficiently strong memory drives the Markov certificate to a horizon-scale window and leaves the universal \(4B^2\) cap as the safer guarantee.  Because the sequential converse is open, these prescriptions are certified upper-bound choices, not yet information-theoretically necessary windows.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The general-horizon prior family is still only a construction handle.  Fixed-scale posterior variance and adaptive assignment-factor cancellation are available, and the constant-path and strict-alternation endpoints are controlled, but arbitrary concatenations of run lengths require a new deterministic inequality coupling random-offset block occupancy to arm-specific positive-part band information.  A dyadic pigeonhole argument would lose \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) if a summed diagnostic lower bound were available; that summed bound has not been proved.  The path \(0000111001110101\) at \(T=16\), \(L=4\) already defeats the naive unit-threshold single-scale dichotomy.  Thus neither a logarithmic lower frontier nor its no-log refinement is currently a theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The optimized Markov upper certificate, its explicit finite-horizon constants, its \(4B^2\) cap, and its radius-aware operational elbows are proved.  The all-policy common-null converse, including the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) version with radius term \(B^2\wedge C^2L^{-2\beta}\), remains open; the no-log frontier theorem is only a conditional implication.  The no-carryover boundary is retained separately.  No unknown-\(\beta\) adaptation, confidence interval, policy-optimality certificate, or sharp leading constant is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the sole prospective root converse: it must prevent every outcome-adaptive cadence from routing around both hidden counterfactual blocks and low-information arm-specific tail bumps.
statement_notes.gap: The strengthened radius target is \(B^2\wedge C^2L^{-2\beta}\).  A dyadic decomposition suggests at most a \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) loss, but the pathwise summed occupancy--information inequality needed to justify that loss is unproved.
statement_notes.consumer: A proved logarithmic certificate would yield an unconditional two-sided bracket with a logarithmic gap; removing the logarithm would then be a distinct open refinement.

statement_notes.justification: This audited constructive theorem minimizes the existing Markov certificate over all integer windows, adds the bounded-parameter cap, and exposes the dependence on the memory-to-outcome radius ratio.
statement_notes.gap: It is an upper certificate for one nonadaptive design and estimator, not a proof that no sequential policy can improve it.
statement_notes.consumer: Experiment owners can enumerate the finite certificate before launch and translate its minimizer into a clock-time window.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem records the mathematical implication of a no-loss sequential multiscale certificate together with the proved upper bound.
statement_notes.gap: Its lower premise is open, so the matched all-policy frontier is conditional and is not part of the proved headline.
statement_notes.consumer: If the multiscale certificate is later closed, this theorem converts it directly into the fixed-radius asymptotic frontier.

statement_notes.justification: This supporting proposition translates the exact certificate minimizer into deployment units and separates the three radius regimes.
statement_notes.gap: It is a known-\(\beta\) upper-bound prescription and makes neither an adaptation claim nor an information-theoretic necessity claim.
statement_notes.consumer: Statsig-style and marketplace switchbacks can pre-register the certified window after specifying the outcome and memory radii.
